{"type":"text","timestamp":1791981767505,"sessionID":"ses_ec592d9b9ffepF2Avmj7MbRoO1","part":{"id":"prt_13a6eb6240011HxF75VMHs4FOH","sessionID":"ses_ec592d9b9ffepF2Avmj7MbRoO1","messageID":"msg_13a6eb216001W1XgtW4l63TDtC","type":"text","text":"---\n\n# Requirements Elicitation Package\n\n## Understanding\n\n**Requested outcome:** The account service sends a password-reset message to a user within a bounded time after the user requests a password reset.\n\n**Proposed system boundary:** The account service — specifically its outbound notification path — at the point where it dispatches the reset message to an external delivery channel.\n\n**Source material:** Two supplied requirements (R1, R2) and a prose gap statement naming three missing behaviors.\n\n**Information sorting:**\n\n| Source statement | Kind |\n|---|---|\n| R1 — account service sends a \"reset message\" within 60 seconds | Behavioral obligation (candidate) |\n| R2 — account service sends a \"password-reset email\" within 1 minute | Behavioral obligation — likely duplicate of R1; medium differs slightly |\n| \"No behavior for an unavailable mail provider\" | Identified gap — failure-path obligation |\n| \"No behavior for repeated requests\" | Identified gap — boundary/lifecycle obligation |\n| \"No behavior for an expired reset link\" | Identified gap — state/lifecycle obligation |\n\n**Key observations before drafting:**\n\n1. **Duplicate or near-duplicate:** R1 (\"reset message\" / 60 seconds) and R2 (\"password-reset email\" / 1 minute) describe the same trigger, the same responsible system, and the same timing limit expressed in different units. They differ only in the word used for the outbound artifact. This is an **overlap / near-duplicate** finding. The intended behavior is ambiguous: are both terms referring to an email, or is \"reset message\" a broader channel (SMS, push, in-app)? This must be resolved before either can be marked ready.\n2. **Timing units are identical in magnitude** (60 s = 1 min) but inconsistently expressed.\n3. **Three gaps** are acknowledged by the submitter: unavailable mail provider, repeated requests, and expired reset link. None of these have requirements.\n\n---\n\n## Clarifying Questions\n\n**Q1 (Duplicate / channel scope — blocks R1 and R2):**\nR1 uses \"reset message\" and R2 uses \"password-reset email.\" Do both requirements describe the same delivery channel (email), making one redundant? Or does \"reset message\" intentionally cover additional channels (e.g., SMS, push)? If multiple channels are intended, is the 60-second deadline per channel or for all channels collectively?\n\n**Q2 (Timing — blocks R1 and R2):**\nShould the 60-second / 1-minute deadline be expressed as a single canonical value and unit? Is the deadline measured from when the account service *receives* the user's request or from when it *begins processing* it?\n\n**Q3 (Mail-provider failure — blocks SR-A):**\nWhen the external mail provider is unavailable, what shall the account service do? Candidates include: retry with a defined schedule, queue the message for later delivery, return an error to the calling interface, or notify the user through an alternate channel. Which behavior is required, and what retry limit or timeout applies?\n\n**Q4 (Repeated requests — blocks SR-B):**\nWhen a user submits multiple password-reset requests before the first link is used or expires, shall the account service honor each independently, invalidate prior pending links, or reject subsequent requests within a window? If rate-limited, what is the limit and the response when exceeded?\n\n**Q5 (Reset-link expiry — blocks SR-C):**\nWhen a user attempts to use a reset link after it has expired, what shall the account service do? What expiry duration is intended?\n\n**Q6 (Audit / confirmation — optional):**\nIs the account service required to record an event (log entry, audit trail) when a reset message is dispatched, when delivery fails, or when a link is used or expires?\n\n---\n\n## Candidate Requirements\n\n### Candidate 1 (from R1)\n\n- **Status:** needs clarification\n- **Template:** Event-driven\n- **Requirement:** When a user requests a password reset, the account service shall dispatch a password-reset [message | email — see Q1] within 60 seconds of receiving the request.\n- **Source intent and rationale:** R1 asserts a bounded latency so users receive the reset credential promptly. The intended channel is unresolved.\n- **Implementability contract**\n  - System boundary: Account service, outbound notification interface.\n  - Responsible system: Account service.\n  - Actor: User (interface — web form, API, etc. — not specified).\n  - Affected interfaces: Account service to external mail/messaging provider; response interface back to caller.\n  - Inputs and data definitions: Password-reset request for an identified user account. \"Reset message\" channel undefined (Q1 open). User identity lookup not defined in R1/R2.\n  - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger: Trigger is user submitting a password-reset request. No precondition on account state (e.g., active, unblocked) is stated.\n  - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response: Normal — reset message dispatched within 60 seconds. Alternate and failure — undefined (Q3, Q4 open).\n  - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances: 60 seconds. Measurement start open (Q2). No tolerance stated.\n  - Domain terms, dependencies, and unresolved decisions: \"Reset message\" vs. \"password-reset email\" (Q1 open). Measurement start (Q2 open). Possible duplicate of Candidate 2.\n- **Verification contract**\n  - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus: Valid user account exists; password-reset request submitted to the account service.\n  - Observable evidence or oracle: Reset message received on the target delivery channel; timestamp of dispatch compared to timestamp of request receipt.\n  - Expected result: Reset message dispatched within 60 seconds of request receipt.\n  - Pass/fail criteria, including scope, thresholds, units, and timing: Pass if dispatch ≤ 60 s from request receipt. Fail otherwise. \"Dispatch\" boundary (internal vs. provider handoff) is open (Q2).\n  - Boundary, negative, and failure cases: No message sent (fail). Message sent after 60 s (fail). Provider unavailable (Q3 open). Repeated requests (Q4 open).\n  - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence: Timestamps at request receipt and at dispatch; account-service outbound log or provider delivery confirmation.\n  - Observable at the named boundary alone: No — the 60-second constraint requires timestamps at both the request-receipt boundary and the dispatch boundary.\n  - If no, internal evidence needed and rationale: Internal request-receipt timestamp and outbound dispatch timestamp both required to measure compliance.\n\n---\n\n### Candidate 2 (from R2)\n\n- **Status:** needs clarification\n- **Template:** Event-driven\n- **Requirement:** When a user requests a password reset, the account service shall dispatch a password-reset email within 60 seconds of receiving the request.\n- **Source intent and rationale:** R2 specifies email as the channel and states a 1-minute (= 60-second) limit. Likely describes the same behavior as R1 with a more specific channel term. Overlap with Candidate 1 is open pending Q1.\n- **Implementability contract**\n  - System boundary: Account service, outbound email interface.\n  - Responsible system: Account service.\n  - Actor: User.\n  - Affected interfaces: Account service to external email provider.\n  - Inputs and data definitions: Password-reset request for a user with a registered email address. Email address validity and lookup not defined.\n  - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger: Same trigger as Candidate 1. No stated precondition on account state.\n  - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response: Normal — email dispatched within 60 seconds. Alternate and failure — undefined (Q3 open).\n  - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances: 60 seconds (1 minute). Measurement start open (Q2). No tolerance stated.\n  - Domain terms, dependencies, and unresolved decisions: \"Password-reset email\" more specific than R1's \"reset message\"; relationship open (Q1). Measurement start (Q2 open). Possible duplicate of Candidate 1.\n- **Verification contract**\n  - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus: Valid user account with registered email address; password-reset request submitted.\n  - Observable evidence or oracle: Password-reset email received in target inbox; dispatch/delivery timestamp compared to request timestamp.\n  - Expected result: Email dispatched within 60 seconds of request receipt.\n  - Pass/fail criteria, including scope, thresholds, units, and timing: Pass if dispatch ≤ 60 s. \"Dispatch\" vs. \"delivery\" boundary open (Q2).\n  - Boundary, negative, and failure cases: No email sent (fail). Email sent after deadline (fail). Email provider unavailable (Q3 open). User has no registered email address (undefined). Repeated requests (Q4 open).\n  - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence: Request-receipt and dispatch timestamps; provider delivery log or test mailbox.\n  - Observable at the named boundary alone: No — same dual-timestamp constraint as Candidate 1.\n  - If no, internal evidence needed and rationale: Internal request-receipt timestamp and outbound dispatch timestamp both required.\n\n---\n\n## Suggested Supporting Requirements\n\n**SR-A — Mail-provider unavailability (Failure-path companion)**\nRelated to Candidates 1 and 2 (normal dispatch path). Provisional sentence pending Q5:\n> If a user submits an expired password-reset link, then the account service shall [return an error / redirect to a new-request flow — to be determined by Q5].\n\n**SR-D — Reset-link expiry duration (Required companion for SR-C)**\nRelated to SR-C. The duration for which a reset link remains valid is not stated in R1 or R2. Without it, SR-C cannot be verified and implementers will choose arbitrary values. Provisional sentence pending Q5:\n> The account service shall invalidate a password-reset link [N minutes/hours — to be determined by Q5] after it is dispatched.\n\n**SR-E — Audit event for dispatch (Optional consideration)**\nRelated to Candidates 1 and 2. Password-reset flows are a common vector for account-takeover attacks. Recording a timestamped event when a reset message is dispatched supports security monitoring and incident investigation. Not implied by R1 or R2; ask whether it is in scope (Q6).\n\n---\n\n## Consistency Findings\n\n### Finding 1 — Duplicate / Overlap: R1 and R2\n\n- **Affected items:** Candidate 1 (R1), Candidate 2 (R2).\n- **Condition:** Identical trigger (user requests a password reset), identical responsible system (account service), identical timing constraint (60 s = 1 min). They differ only in the label for the outbound artifact: \"reset message\" vs. \"password-reset email.\"\n- **Consequence:** If both terms denote the same channel, the requirements are near-identical duplicates that will diverge as they are maintained separately. If \"reset message\" is intentionally broader, the two requirements overlap on the email channel and may impose two independent obligations, risking double dispatch.\n- **Resolution options:**\n  1. Confirm both refer to email → consolidate into one requirement using \"password-reset email.\"\n  2. Confirm \"reset message\" covers multiple channels → scope each requirement to its channel, one per channel or one covering all configured channels.\n- **Blocks:** Both candidates remain `needs clarification` until Q1 is answered.\n\n### Finding 2 — Gap: No failure path for provider unavailability\n\n- **Affected items:** Candidates 1 and 2.\n- **Condition:** Both candidates require dispatch within 60 seconds, but no requirement exists for what happens if the external provider is unavailable during that window.\n- **Consequence:** An implementer cannot make a conforming choice. A verifier cannot determine pass or fail for a test with a simulated provider outage.\n- **Resolution options:** Add SR-A with the answer to Q3.\n\n### Finding 3 — Gap: No behavior for repeated reset requests\n\n- **Affected items:** Candidates 1 and 2.\n- **Condition:** The trigger does not specify whether it applies once per pending reset or on every invocation. Multiple valid reset tokens could coexist with undefined precedence.\n- **Consequence:** Two implementers could produce different security postures for the same trigger.\n- **Resolution options:** Add SR-B with the answer to Q4.\n\n### Finding 4 — Gap: No reset-link lifecycle behavior\n\n- **Affected items:** Candidates 1 and 2 (downstream of dispatch).\n- **Condition:** Neither requirement defines how long a dispatched reset link remains valid or what happens when an expired link is submitted.\n- **Consequence:** The reset flow is incomplete. A user who receives a link but delays acting has no defined outcome.\n- **Resolution options:** Add SR-C and SR-D with the answers to Q5.\n\n---\n\n## Assumptions\n\n**A1 (Provisional):** \"Reset message\" in R1 and \"password-reset email\" in R2 refer to the same delivery channel (email). Provisional pending Q1. If wrong, separate channel-scoped candidates are needed.\n\n**A2 (Provisional):** The 60-second and 1-minute constraints are identical in magnitude. Canonical unit going forward is 60 seconds. # Requirements Elicitation Package

## Understanding

**Requested outcome:** The report should display a warning to users when its
content may be out of date (stale). The product owner has not yet decided two
material facts: (1) how old a report must be before it is considered stale, and
(2) whether the warning is mandatory (always shown when the threshold is met) or
optional (can be dismissed or suppressed).

**Proposed system boundary:** The report (a named system component or UI
surface) is responsible for displaying the staleness warning. The report is
treated as the single responsible system unless additional information
establishes that a separate service, scheduler, or notification subsystem owns
this behavior.

**Source type:** This is a partial goal statement with two explicitly
unresolved product decisions. It is not a normative obligation yet. The
uncertainty is acknowledged by the product owner and must not be resolved by
assumption.

---

## Clarifying Questions

**Q1 — Staleness threshold (blocking)**
What age threshold makes a report stale? For example: more than 24 hours since
last data refresh, more than N business days since generation, or some other
measurable criterion? The implementability contract and verification contract
cannot be completed without this value and its units.

**Q2 — Mandatory vs. optional warning (blocking)**
Must the warning appear whenever the threshold is met (mandatory, with no
user-dismissal path), or may the user dismiss or suppress it? This determines
whether the requirement is an unconditional obligation or a conditional one, and
whether a separate requirement is needed to govern dismissal.

**Q3 — Warning content and form**
What does the warning communicate? For example, must it state the data age, the
threshold, a last-refresh timestamp, or only a generic "may be stale" label?
This affects implementability and verification.

**Q4 — Report identity**
Does "the report" refer to a single report type, every report in the system, or
a configurable subset? If multiple report types exist, does the staleness rule
apply uniformly?

**Q5 — What clock or event defines age?**
Is age measured from the time the underlying data was last refreshed, the time
the report was generated, or another observable event? Two implementers may
choose differently without this definition.

---

## Candidate Requirements

### Candidate 1

- **Status:** needs clarification
- **Template:** unresolved — cannot select between Event-driven, State-driven,
  Unwanted behavior, or Ubiquitous without knowing whether the warning is
  mandatory, what triggers it, and what threshold defines "stale."
- **Requirement:** *(Drafting is blocked. A provisional sketch is shown below
  for review only — it is not a normative sentence.)*

  > Provisional sketch (not normative): While the report data age exceeds
  > [THRESHOLD — undefined], the report shall display a staleness warning.

  The bracketed value is a material open decision. The EARS pattern, the
  normative sentence, and both contracts cannot be finalized until Q1 and Q2
  are answered.

- **Source intent and rationale:** The product owner wants users to know when
  the report content may not reflect current data, reducing the risk of
  decisions based on stale information. The product owner has not committed to
  a threshold or to whether the warning is always shown.

- **Implementability contract**
  - System boundary: The report surface (UI, document, or API response — form
    not yet established).
  - Responsible system: The report.
  - Actor: The user viewing the report.
  - Affected interfaces: The report display interface (visual, document, or
    API). Specific interface not yet defined.
  - Inputs and data definitions: A measurable "data age" value — the elapsed
    time since an observable reference event (Q5). **Open: reference event
    undefined.**
  - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger: The condition that makes
    a report stale. **Open: staleness threshold and units undefined (Q1).**
  - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response: Display of a staleness
    warning. **Open: mandatory vs. optional undefined (Q2); warning content
    undefined (Q3).**
  - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances: **Open:
    threshold value and units undefined (Q1).**
  - Domain terms, dependencies, and unresolved decisions: "Stale," "warning,"
    "data age," "mandatory," "report" — all unresolved. See Q1–Q5.

- **Verification contract**
  - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus: **Open: cannot specify setup
    without the threshold (Q1) and the reference event (Q5).**
  - Observable evidence or oracle: The presence or absence of a staleness
    warning on the report surface.
  - Expected result: Warning is displayed when data age exceeds the threshold.
    **Open: pass/fail boundary undefined.**
  - Pass/fail criteria, including scope, thresholds, units, and timing:
    **Open: threshold undefined (Q1).**
  - Boundary, negative, and failure cases: Case where age equals threshold
    exactly (boundary); case where age is below threshold (warning absent);
    case where age data is unavailable. All unresolvable without Q1 and Q5.
  - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence: A
    verifiable timestamp or elapsed-time value observable at the report
    boundary.
  - Observable at the named boundary alone: yes — the warning is a visible
    property of the report surface, provided the age value is also observable
    there.
  - If no, internal evidence needed and rationale: N/A (boundary-observable,
    subject to the age value being surfaced).

---

## Suggested Supporting Requirements

**SR-A — Boundary companion** (relates to Candidate 1)
*Missing behavior:* What the report shall do when the data age cannot be
determined (e.g., no timestamp is available). Without this, two implementers
would make different choices: one suppresses the warning, one shows it
unconditionally.
*Suggestion:* If the report cannot determine whether its data is current, then
the report shall display a staleness warning.
*Reason:* Absence of an age value is arguably the most conservative case for
staleness and should be explicitly addressed before implementation.

**SR-B — Required companion** (relates to Candidate 1, conditional on Q2)
*Missing behavior:* If the warning is determined to be dismissible (Q2 =
optional), a requirement is needed to define how and for how long a user may
suppress the warning, and whether the warning reappears on the next session or
the next threshold crossing.
*Suggestion:* Add a companion requirement governing dismissal scope, persistence,
and re-display conditions once the mandatory/optional decision is made.
*Reason:* Without this companion, the dismissal behavior is undefined and
two implementers will produce different results.

**SR-C — Operational companion** (relates to Candidate 1)
*Missing behavior:* The report data-age value must be observable at the report
boundary for the staleness condition to be verifiable. If the age is not
currently surfaced, a requirement to expose it may be needed.
*Suggestion:* Consider whether a separate requirement is needed for the report
to expose the data-refresh timestamp (or computed age) so that the staleness
condition can be independently verified.
*Reason:* Without an observable age value, the staleness warning cannot be
verified by an evaluator examining only the report boundary.

---

## Consistency Findings

**Finding 1 — Gap: threshold is undefined**
Candidate 1 cannot be reconciled with any other system behavior because the
staleness threshold is not defined. If a threshold is later introduced in a
different requirement (e.g., a data-refresh SLA), it should be confirmed
whether the staleness definition here must align with that value.

**Finding 2 — Precedence question: mandatory vs. optional**
If the warning is optional (Q2), an explicit precedence is needed between the
"show warning" obligation and any user preference or role-based permission to
suppress it. Without this, two valid interpretations conflict: one always shows
the warning to all users, one respects user-level suppression settings.

No conflicts or duplicates exist in the current candidate set because only one
candidate has been drafted.

---

## Assumptions

**A1 (provisional):** "The report" refers to a single, identifiable system
component or UI surface. If multiple report types exist, this assumption must
be revisited.

**A2 (provisional):** "Age" is a duration measured from a single observable
reference event (e.g., last data refresh). If age is derived from multiple
events, the calculation rule must be defined.

**A3 (provisional):** The staleness condition is evaluated at report-display
time, not at a scheduled interval. This assumption affects whether the
requirement is event-driven (triggered by display) or state-driven (maintained
continuously). It must be confirmed by the product owner.

---

## Rationale and Context

The product owner's intent is to protect users from acting on outdated report
data. The warning is the proposed mechanism. The product owner has explicitly
deferred two decisions: the staleness threshold and whether the warning is
mandatory. These are not implementation details; they are normative policy
choices that determine the EARS pattern, the normative sentence, and the
verification criteria. They must be resolved before a normative requirement
can be finalized.

Split\n  `shall ... and shall ...` or independently testable responses into separate\n  candidates before returning the package.\n- If the EARS pattern cannot be selected without guessing, use `Template:\n  unresolved`, explain the blocking question, and do not invent a normative\n  sentence.\n\n## Accepted Inputs\n\nThe input may be any of the following:\n\n- A goal or problem statement.\n- A feature request or interface description.\n- One existing requirement to review or revise.\n- A set of requirements to compare for consistency.\n- A mixture of prose, requirement records, IDs, tags, trace links, and review\n  metadata from a host system.\n\nIf the input contains several artifacts, first identify what each artifact is.\nDo not assume that an existing requirement is correct, that a design proposal\nis a requirement, or that a test description is the only possible\nimplementation.\n\n## Separate the Information\n\nBefore drafting, sort source statements into these buckets:\n\n| Kind | Meaning | Treatment |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Goal | The outcome the requester wants | Restate it; do not present it as system behavior yet |\n| Rationale | Why the outcome matters | Preserve separately from the normative sentence |\n| Constraint | A limit imposed by the domain, user, environment, or policy | Confirm its scope and whether it is normative |\n| Assumption | An interpretation not established by the source | Label as provisional and ask when material |\n| Design idea | A proposed way to implement the outcome | Keep separate; do not leak it into the requirement |\n| Behavioral obligation | What a named system must make observable | Candidate for an EARS requirement |\n| Question | An unresolved choice or missing fact | Ask it or mark the candidate as needing clarification |\n| Evidence | A fact, artifact, measurement, or source used to support a claim | Cite or identify it; do not confuse it with the obligation |\n\nState the requested outcome and the proposed system boundary in plain language\nbefore presenting requirements. If either is unclear, say what is unclear and\nask the smallest question that will resolve it.\n\n## EARS Model\n\nEARS means Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax. Choose a pattern for its\nmeaning, not for a keyword that happens to occur in the source.\n\n### Structural rules\n\nUse this clause order when more than one conditional clause is needed:\n\n```text\nWhile <optional precondition(s)>, when <optional trigger>,\nthe <system name> shall <system response>.\n```\n\nEnforce these rules:\n\n- Zero or more preconditions may scope an obligation.\n- Zero or one trigger may start the obligation.\n- Each requirement names exactly one responsible system.\n- Each requirement has at least one externally observable system response.\n- Clause order is meaningful: a precondition holds before a trigger, and the\n  response is required only in the stated scope.\n- Use one normative `shall` obligation per requirement whenever obligations can\n  be negotiated or verified independently. Split independent responses even\n  when the source joins them with `and`.\n- Put actors, external systems, inputs, and affected interfaces in the\n  conditions or context unless one named system is clearly responsible for the\n  response.\n\n### The six patterns\n\n| Pattern | Canonical template | Select it when |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Ubiquitous | `The <system> shall <response>.` | The obligation is unconditional and always active. |\n| Event-driven | `When <trigger>, the <system> shall <response>.` | A discrete event at the boundary starts the behavior. |\n| State-driven | `While <state>, the <system> shall <response>.` | The obligation remains active throughout a defined state. Interpret `During` as a source/readability synonym, but use `While` in canonical output. |\n| Optional feature | `Where <feature is included>, the <system> shall <response>.` | The behavior exists only when an optional capability is included in the product. |\n| Unwanted behavior | `If <undesired condition>, then the <system> shall <response>.` | A failure, error, disturbance, deviation, or other unwanted situation requires a response. |\n| Complex | `While <precondition>, when <trigger>, the <system> shall <response>.` | Multiple conditions are genuinely required for one obligation. |\n\nThe complex form is a combination of conditions, not a default form. If the\nstate, event, optional capability, or unwanted condition describes an\nindependent obligation, split it into separate requirements instead.\n\n## Detailed Guidance\n\nRead [references/ears-and-review.md](references/ears-and-review.md) for pattern\ndistinctions and examples, drafting checks, readiness contracts, supporting\nrequirements, consistency analysis, and the exact portable response shape.\n\nThe short rule is: ask rather than guess, keep unresolved candidates at\n`needs clarification`, and require observable implementability and verification\ncontracts before `ready for review`. Check each candidate independently: if its\ncontract says `open`, `unresolved`, `pending`, or `incomplete`, that candidate\nmust not be `candidate` or `ready for review`.\n\n## Supporting Requirements and Language\n\nRead [references/quality-guidance.md](references/quality-guidance.md) when drafting supporting requirements or\napplying controlled-language guidance. The guidance keeps ASD-STE100-inspired\nstyle separate from the normative EARS rules and preserves uncertainty.\n\n## Elicitation Loop\n\nWork iteratively. For each pass:\n\n1. Restate the requested outcome and proposed system boundary.\n2. Identify actors, external systems, interfaces, data, states, optional\n   capabilities, and explicit constraints.\n3. Separate goals, rationale, assumptions, design ideas, and obligations.\n4. Select an EARS pattern from the meaning of each obligation.\n5. Draft candidate requirements and split independent behavior.\n6. Ask only the highest-value questions needed to remove ambiguity.\n7. Add measurable details and update both quality contracts.\n8. Suggest grounded supporting requirements, with their relationship to the\n   source.\n9. Analyze the candidate set for consistency.\n10. Present review status and unresolved items.\n\nOn the next turn, use the user's answers to revise the candidates and rerun\nboth contracts and the consistency analysis. If the user does not answer a\nmaterial question, retain `needs clarification`.\n\n### High-value questions\n\nPrefer a small set of specific questions over a generic request for more\ndetail. Ask about:\n\n- The system boundary and responsibility when more than one system is named.\n- The actor, affected interface, input, identity, or external dependency.\n- Whether a condition is an event, state, optional capability, or unwanted\n  situation.\n- The measurable response, oracle, timing, units, limits, or tolerance.\n- Invalid, missing, duplicate, concurrent, out-of-order, timeout, retry,\n  cancellation, recovery, and partial-completion behavior when applicable.\n- The definition of an ambiguous domain term or lifecycle state.\n- The intended exception or precedence when requirements overlap.\n\nDo not ask about a quality attribute merely because it is common. Ask about\nperformance, security, privacy, accessibility, localization, compatibility,\nretention, auditability, or observability when the request or its boundary\nimplies it.\n\n## Output Discipline\n\nUse the exact headings and status/template fields in\n[references/ears-and-review.md](references/ears-and-review.md). The durable output is a\nportable requirements package that a person or another agent can review,\nimplement, and verify without guessing material behavior.\n\nThis is a general-purpose, host-independent capability. It is not a product workflow, a\nrequirements database, an approval process, an architecture decision, a code\ngenerator, a Gherkin generator, or a host-specific agent workflow.\n\n## Operating Rules\n\nFollow these rules on every invocation:\n\n1. Preserve the user's intended behavior. Do not silently add policy, priority,\n   precedence, scope, or error behavior.\n2. Ask a focused question when a missing fact could cause two reasonable\n   implementers or verifiers to choose different behavior. Never hide that\n   uncertainty in a confident sentence.\n6. A syntactically valid EARS sentence is only a candidate. Mark it `ready for\nreview` only after both quality contracts in the\n[readiness gate](references/ears-and-review.md#readiness-gate)\n   pass.\n7. Suggestions and assumptions remain visibly separate from candidate\n   requirements. A suggestion is not an approved requirement.\n8. Approval, persistence, identifiers, tags, trace links, persisted\n   relationships, and lifecycle states belong to the host. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1791981772870,"sessionID":"ses_ec5903378ffedLI7p71UGYWhQJ","part":{"partID":"prt_13a6fda280015bILhtXGL0QJeO","sessionID":"ses_ec5903378ffedLI7p71UGYWhQJ","messageID":"msg_13a6fd2f1001J6pe556lGA6BEv","type":"tool","id":"toolu_vrtx_016ecsFozzxgn3UKgDqGFCKW","tool":"read","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"path":"/Users/ricmitch/Code/ProtoBot/.worktrees/agent/63-calibrate-eval-baseline/.agents/skills/eliciting-requirements/references/ears-and-review.md"},"output":"Read file /Users/ricmitch/Code/ProtoBot/.worktrees/agent/63-calibrate-eval-baseline/.agents/skills/eliciting-requirements/references/ears-and-review.md, lines 1-252\n1: # EARS and Review Reference\n2: \n3: Read this reference when the main skill's compact workflow needs detailed\n4: pattern selection, readiness contracts, supporting requirements, consistency\n5: analysis, or response formatting.\n6: \n7: ## Pattern Selection\n8: \n9: Choose an EARS pattern for its meaning, not for a keyword in the source.\n10: \n11: - Use `When` for a discrete boundary event, not an enduring state.\n12: - Use `While` for a state-driven requirement. Interpret `During` as an ongoing\n13:   state or precondition in source material, but normalize it to `While` in the\n14:   drafted requirement.\n15: - Use `Where` only for an optional capability included in the product, not an\n16:   ordinary runtime branch.\n17: - Use `If ... then` for an unwanted failure, error, disturbance, deviation, or\n18:   recovery condition.\n19: - Use the ubiquitous form only when no condition limits the obligation.\n20: - Use the complex form only when all conditions are genuinely required for one\n21:   obligation. Split independent obligations instead.\n22: \n23: If the pattern cannot be selected without guessing, use `unresolved`, ask the\n24: pattern question, and keep the candidate `needs clarification`.\n25: \n26: ### Canonical examples\n27: \n28: 1. **Ubiquitous:** `The account service shall record the account identifier\n29:    for every accepted account.` The obligation is unconditional.\n30: 2. **Event-driven:** `When a client submits a valid order, the order service\n31:    shall return an order identifier.` Submission is a discrete event.\n32: 3. **State-driven:** `While the device is in maintenance mode, the controller\n33:    shall inhibit remote actuation.` The obligation lasts for the state.\n34: 4. **Optional feature:** `Where offline export is included, the export\n35:    service shall provide the current report as a downloadable file.` The\n36:    behavior depends on product configuration.\n37: 5. **Unwanted behavior:** `If an authorization check fails, then the gateway\n38:    shall deny the requested operation without disclosing protected data.`\n39: 6. **Complex:** `While the aircraft is on-ground, when reverse thrust is\n40:    commanded, the control system shall enable deployment of the thrust\n41:    reverser.` Both conditions are needed for this response.\n42: \n43: An in-flight reverse-thrust command is a separate unwanted or state/event\n44: requirement, not an exception hidden in the on-ground sentence.\n45: \n46: When an unwanted condition is nested in a state-and-event scope, prefer a\n47: separate `If ... then` requirement. Do not call a `While ... when ...`\n48: sentence unwanted behavior without the unwanted-condition form.\n49: \n50: ## Candidate Quality\n51: \n52: Draft the smallest EARS sentence that preserves intent. If a contract is\n53: incomplete but the pattern is known, show a provisional sentence with the\n54: unresolved condition or value explicitly marked and use `needs clarification`.\n55: \n56: Check:\n57: \n58: - System boundary.\n59: - Responsible system.\n60: - Actor.\n61: - Affected interfaces.\n62: - Explicit trigger, state, feature scope, or unwanted condition.\n63: - Observable response with a concrete verb.\n64: - Defined or questioned inputs, identities, data, domain, and lifecycle terms.\n65: - Quantities, units, limits, ranges, rates, ordering, deadlines, durations, and\n66:   tolerances when material.\n67: - Alternate, failure, cancellation, timeout, retry, recovery, and partial\n68:   completion behavior when material.\n69: - Empty, minimum, maximum, duplicate, concurrent, and out-of-order cases when\n70:   implied.\n71: - No internal classes, functions, storage, frameworks, prompts, or algorithms\n72:   in the normative sentence.\n73: - No passive voice that hides the actor, unclear pronouns, unbounded lists,\n74:   mixed rationale/design/obligation, stacked clauses, or nominalizations that\n75:   hide independent decisions.\n76: \n77: Use temporary labels such as `Candidate 1` for unlabeled input. Preserve host\n78: IDs, tags, and trace links exactly. When revising an existing requirement show\n79: the source, the proposed revision, and the risk removed.\n80: \n81: ## Readiness Gate\n82: \n83: Do not mark `ready for review` unless both contracts pass. This status is not\n84: approval.\n85: \n86: ### Implementability contract\n87: \n88: Record, or explicitly mark not applicable:\n89: \n90: - System boundary.\n91: - Responsible system.\n92: - Actor.\n93: - Affected interfaces.\n94: - Inputs and data definitions.\n95: - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger.\n96: - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response.\n97: - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances.\n98: - Domain terms and dependencies an implementer would otherwise guess.\n99: - Material unresolved decisions and conflicts.\n100: \n101: The contract fails when a material item is unknown or two reasonable\n102: implementations could differ in visible behavior.\n103: \n104: ### Verification contract\n105: \n106: Record:\n107: \n108: - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus.\n109: - Observable evidence or oracle.\n110: - Expected result.\n111: - Explicit pass/fail criteria, including scope, thresholds, units, and timing.\n112: - Boundary, negative, and failure cases when material.\n113: - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence.\n114: - Whether the requirement is observable at the named boundary alone; if not,\n115:   the internal evidence needed and why.\n116: \n117: The contract fails when an evaluator cannot tell what to observe, what result\n118: is expected, or what counts as pass or fail.\n119: \n120: Describe observability without choosing a host-specific verification mode. A\n121: host may map the answer to its own verification metadata.\n122: \n123: Use exactly these statuses:\n124: \n125: - `needs clarification`: a material question, conflict, undefined term, or\n126:   incomplete contract remains.\n127: - `candidate`: both contracts are complete, but the host has not approved the\n128:   draft.\n129: - `ready for review`: both contracts pass and no material finding blocks\n130:   review; this is not approval.\n131: \n132: These statuses describe the elicitation response. They are not persisted\n133: requirement lifecycle states.\n134: \n135: Use `needs clarification` for an incomplete contract. These claims fail the\n136: gate until refined:\n137: \n138: - `The UI must be responsive.` Ask for interaction, workload, device scope,\n139:   response-time measure, and pass/fail observation.\n140: - `The system must not contain security vulnerabilities.` Ask for threat scope,\n141:   vulnerability classes, assessment method, severity threshold, and release\n142:   boundary. Decompose it into observable behaviors and scoped assurance\n143:   criteria.\n144: \n145: Flag `quickly`, `appropriately`, `user-friendly`, `as needed`, `normally`,\n146: `securely`, `support`, `handle`, `etc.`, and `reasonable` unless each has an\n147: agreed measure. Preserve the source rationale separately.\n148: \n149: ## Supporting Requirements\n150: \n151: Suggestions must name the source behavior, missing behavior, relationship, and\n152: reason. Keep them outside the candidate list until accepted.\n153: \n154: The relationship labels below describe the role of a suggested companion in\n155: this response. They are not a persistent requirements-store relationship\n156: vocabulary. Do not invent stable IDs or persisted edges; preserve host-supplied\n157: metadata and let the host map these labels when it defines a mapping. When\n158: revising an identified requirement, show its source and proposed revision\n159: rather than inferring a relationship that the host did not provide.\n160: \n161: Use these relationship labels:\n162: \n163: - **Required companion:** needed for completeness.\n164: - **Failure-path companion:** defines material failure or recovery.\n165: - **Boundary companion:** defines an implied limit or edge case.\n166: - **Interface companion:** defines behavior at a system or external boundary.\n167: - **Operational companion:** defines an observable operational quality implied\n168:   by the request.\n169: - **Optional consideration:** plausible but not justified; ask whether it is in\n170:   scope.\n171: \n172: Consider normal, alternate, negative, recovery, validation, missing or\n173: malformed values, duplicates, boundaries, lifecycle, authentication,\n174: authorization, ownership, persistence, consistency, idempotence, ordering,\n175: concurrency, dependency failures, timeouts, retries, cancellation, partial\n176: completion, performance, capacity, latency, availability, rate limits,\n177: security, privacy, auditability, retention, accessibility, localization,\n178: compatibility, and observability only when grounded in the source.\n179: \n180: ## Consistency Analysis\n181: \n182: Normalize each candidate by system, feature scope, preconditions, states,\n183: trigger or unwanted condition, response, timing, quantities, ranges, ordering,\n184: quality constraints, and host or temporary ID. Compare conditions semantically,\n185: not only textually.\n186: \n187: Report these finding kinds when present:\n188: \n189: - **Conflict:** applicable requirements cannot both be satisfied.\n190: - **Overlap:** requirements may describe the same behavior.\n191: - **Duplicate:** same or near-identical requirements may drift.\n192: - **Gap:** an important behavior is undefined.\n193: - **Precedence question:** exception or evaluation order is undefined.\n194: - **Intentional exception:** an explicit state, feature, priority, or exception\n195:   resolves an apparent conflict.\n196: - **Infeasible, vacuous, or unreachable:** the condition or obligation cannot\n197:   be meaningfully exercised.\n198: \n199: Check contradictory responses, normal/failure overlap, state/event overlap,\n200: inconsistent units/ranges/deadlines/retries/cardinalities, allow/forbid\n201: contradictions, optional-feature conflicts, incompatible interface contracts,\n202: and missing boundary/failure/lifecycle behavior.\n203: \n204: Every finding shows affected labels or excerpts, conditions, consequence, and\n205: focused resolution options. Options include narrowing, splitting, an explicit\n206: exception, precedence, consolidation, or asking the user to choose. Do not turn verification contracts into\n252: Gherkin or implementation-specific test steps.","title":"read","metadata":{"metadata":{"truncated":false},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Read file /Users/ricmitch/Code/ProtoBot/.worktrees/agent/63-calibrate-eval-baseline/.agents/skills/eliciting-requirements/references/ears-and-review.md, lines 1-252\n1: # EARS and Review Reference\n2: \n3: Read this reference when the main skill's compact workflow needs detailed\n4: pattern selection, readiness contracts, supporting requirements, consistency\n5: analysis, or response formatting.\n6: \n7: ## Pattern Selection\n8: \n9: Choose an EARS pattern for its meaning, not for a keyword in the source.\n10: \n11: - Use `When` for a discrete boundary event, not an enduring state.\n12: - Use `While` for a state-driven requirement. Interpret `During` as an ongoing\n13:   state or precondition in source material, but normalize it to `While` in the\n14:   drafted requirement.\n15: - Use `Where` only for an optional capability included in the product, not an\n16:   ordinary runtime branch.\n17: - Use `If ... then` for an unwanted failure, error, disturbance, deviation, or\n18:   recovery condition.\n19: - Use the ubiquitous form only when no condition limits the obligation.\n20: - Use the complex form only when all conditions are genuinely required for one\n21:   obligation. Split independent obligations instead.\n22: \n23: If the pattern cannot be selected without guessing, use `unresolved`, ask the\n24: pattern question, and keep the candidate `needs clarification`.\n25: \n26: ### Canonical examples\n27: \n28: 1. **Ubiquitous:** `The account service shall record the account identifier\n29:    for every accepted account.` The obligation is unconditional.\n30: 2. **Event-driven:** `When a client submits a valid order, the order service\n31:    shall return an order identifier.` Submission is a discrete event.\n32: 3. **State-driven:** `While the device is in maintenance mode, the controller\n33:    shall inhibit remote actuation.` The obligation lasts for the state.\n34: 4. **Optional feature:** `Where offline export is included, the export\n35:    service shall provide the current report as a downloadable file.` The\n36:    behavior depends on product configuration.\n37: 5. **Unwanted behavior:** `If an authorization check fails, then the gateway\n38:    shall deny the requested operation without disclosing protected data.`\n39: 6. **Complex:** `While the aircraft is on-ground, when reverse thrust is\n40:    commanded, the control system shall enable deployment of the thrust\n41:    reverser.` Both conditions are needed for this response.\n42: \n43: An in-flight reverse-thrust command is a separate unwanted or state/event\n44: requirement, not an exception hidden in the on-ground sentence.\n45: \n46: When an unwanted condition is nested in a state-and-event scope, prefer a\n47: separate `If ... then` requirement. Do not call a `While ... when ...`\n48: sentence unwanted behavior without the unwanted-condition form.\n49: \n50: ## Candidate Quality\n51: \n52: Draft the smallest EARS sentence that preserves intent. If a contract is\n53: incomplete but the pattern is known, show a provisional sentence with the\n54: unresolved condition or value explicitly marked and use `needs clarification`.\n55: \n56: Check:\n57: \n58: - System boundary.\n59: - Responsible system.\n60: - Actor.\n61: - Affected interfaces.\n62: - Explicit trigger, state, feature scope, or unwanted condition.\n63: - Observable response with a concrete verb.\n64: - Defined or questioned inputs, identities, data, domain, and lifecycle terms.\n65: - Quantities, units, limits, ranges, rates, ordering, deadlines, durations, and\n66:   tolerances when material.\n67: - Alternate, failure, cancellation, timeout, retry, recovery, and partial\n68:   completion behavior when material.\n69: - Empty, minimum, maximum, duplicate, concurrent, and out-of-order cases when\n70:   implied.\n71: - No internal classes, functions, storage, frameworks, prompts, or algorithms\n72:   in the normative sentence.\n73: - No passive voice that hides the actor, unclear pronouns, unbounded lists,\n74:   mixed rationale/design/obligation, stacked clauses, or nominalizations that\n75:   hide independent decisions.\n76: \n77: Use temporary labels such as `Candidate 1` for unlabeled input. Preserve host\n78: IDs, tags, and trace links exactly. When revising an existing requirement show\n79: the source, the proposed revision, and the risk removed.\n80: \n81: ## Readiness Gate\n82: \n83: Do not mark `ready for review` unless both contracts pass. This status is not\n84: approval.\n85: \n86: ### Implementability contract\n87: \n88: Record, or explicitly mark not applicable:\n89: \n90: - System boundary.\n91: - Responsible system.\n92: - Actor.\n93: - Affected interfaces.\n94: - Inputs and data definitions.\n95: - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger.\n96: - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response.\n97: - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances.\n98: - Domain terms and dependencies an implementer would otherwise guess.\n99: - Material unresolved decisions and conflicts.\n100: \n101: The contract fails when a material item is unknown or two reasonable\n102: implementations could differ in visible behavior.\n103: \n104: ### Verification contract\n105: \n106: Record:\n107: \n108: - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus.\n109: - Observable evidence or oracle.\n110: - Expected result.\n111: - Explicit pass/fail criteria, including scope, thresholds, units, and timing.\n112: - Boundary, negative, and failure cases when material.\n113: - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence.\n114: - Whether the requirement is observable at the named boundary alone; if not,\n115:   the internal evidence needed and why.\n116: \n117: The contract fails when an evaluator cannot tell what to observe, what result\n118: is expected, or what counts as pass or fail.\n119: \n120: Describe observability without choosing a host-specific verification mode. A\n121: host may map the answer to its own verification metadata.\n122: \n123: Use exactly these statuses:\n124: \n125: - `needs clarification`: a material question, conflict, undefined term, or\n126:   incomplete contract remains.\n127: - `candidate`: both contracts are complete, but the host has not approved the\n128:   draft.\n129: - `ready for review`: both contracts pass and no material finding blocks\n130:   review; this is not approval.\n131: \n132: These statuses describe the elicitation response. They are not persisted\n133: requirement lifecycle states.\n134: \n135: Use `needs clarification` for an incomplete contract. These claims fail the\n136: gate until refined:\n137: \n138: - `The UI must be responsive.` Ask for interaction, workload, device scope,\n139:   response-time measure, and pass/fail observation.\n140: - `The system must not contain security vulnerabilities.` Ask for threat scope,\n141:   vulnerability classes, assessment method, severity threshold, and release\n142:   boundary. Decompose it into observable behaviors and scoped assurance\n143:   criteria.\n144: \n145: Flag `quickly`, `appropriately`, `user-friendly`, `as needed`, `normally`,\n146: `securely`, `support`, `handle`, `etc.`, and `reasonable` unless each has an\n147: agreed measure. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1791981834447,"sessionID":"ses_ec5903378ffedLI7p71UGYWhQJ","part":{"partID":"prt_13a6ff62a001VCnbIZnqQf3CGJ","sessionID":"ses_ec5903378ffedLI7p71UGYWhQJ","messageID":"msg_13a6ff235001n1XkysaxHEMCCJ","type":"tool","id":"toolu_vrtx_01BSJYqkMhNgKavfGynQNYA6","tool":"write","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"path":"/private/var/folders/qm/d729jn6n47z5nxpkpf361l9w0000gn/T/agent-eval/v2-regression/cases/case-014-uncertainty/artifacts/result.md","content":"# Requirements Elicitation Package\n\n## Understanding\n\n**Requested outcome:** The report should display a warning to users when its\ncontent may be out of date (stale). The product owner has not yet decided two\nmaterial facts: (1) how old a report must be before it is considered stale, and\n(2) whether the warning is mandatory (always shown when the threshold is met) or\noptional (can be dismissed or suppressed).\n\n**Proposed system boundary:** The report (a named system component or UI\nsurface) is responsible for displaying the staleness warning. The report is\ntreated as the single responsible system unless additional information\nestablishes that a separate service, scheduler, or notification subsystem owns\nthis behavior.\n\n**Source type:** This is a partial goal statement with two explicitly\nunresolved product decisions. It is not a normative obligation yet. The\nuncertainty is acknowledged by the product owner and must not be resolved by\nassumption.\n\n---\n\n## Clarifying Questions\n\n**Q1 — Staleness threshold (blocking)**\nWhat age threshold makes a report stale? For example: more than 24 hours since\nlast data refresh, more than N business days since generation, or some other\nmeasurable criterion? The implementability contract and verification contract\ncannot be completed without this value and its units.\n\n**Q2 — Mandatory vs. optional warning (blocking)**\nMust the warning appear whenever the threshold is met (mandatory, with no\nuser-dismissal path), or may the user dismiss or suppress it? This determines\nwhether the requirement is an unconditional obligation or a conditional one, and\nwhether a separate requirement is needed to govern dismissal.\n\n**Q3 — Warning content and form**\nWhat does the warning communicate? For example, must it state the data age, the\nthreshold, a last-refresh timestamp, or only a generic \"may be stale\" label?\nThis affects implementability and verification.\n\n**Q4 — Report identity**\nDoes \"the report\" refer to a single report type, every report in the system, or\na configurable subset? If multiple report types exist, does the staleness rule\napply uniformly?\n\n**Q5 — What clock or event defines age?**\nIs age measured from the time the underlying data was last refreshed, the time\nthe report was generated, or another observable event? Two implementers may\nchoose differently without this definition.\n\n---\n\n## Candidate Requirements\n\n### Candidate 1\n\n- **Status:** needs clarification\n- **Template:** unresolved — cannot select between Event-driven, State-driven,\n  Unwanted behavior, or Ubiquitous without knowing whether the warning is\n  mandatory, what triggers it, and what threshold defines \"stale.\"\n- **Requirement:** *(Drafting is blocked. A provisional sketch is shown below\n  for review only — it is not a normative sentence.)*\n\n  > Provisional sketch (not normative): While the report data age exceeds\n  > [THRESHOLD — undefined], the report shall display a staleness warning.\n\n  The bracketed value is a material open decision. The EARS pattern, the\n  normative sentence, and both contracts cannot be finalized until Q1 and Q2\n  are answered.\n\n- **Source intent and rationale:** The product owner wants users to know when\n  the report content may not reflect current data, reducing the risk of\n  decisions based on stale information. The product owner has not committed to\n  a threshold or to whether the warning is always shown.\n\n- **Implementability contract**\n  - System boundary: The report surface (UI, document, or API response — form\n    not yet established).\n  - Responsible system: The report.\n  - Actor: The user viewing the report.\n  - Affected interfaces: The report display interface (visual, document, or\n    API). Specific interface not yet defined.\n  - Inputs and data definitions: A measurable \"data age\" value — the elapsed\n    time since an observable reference event (Q5). **Open: reference event\n    undefined.**\n  - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger: The condition that makes\n    a report stale. **Open: staleness threshold and units undefined (Q1).**\n  - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response: Display of a staleness\n    warning. **Open: mandatory vs. optional undefined (Q2); warning content\n    undefined (Q3).**\n  - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances: **Open:\n    threshold value and units undefined (Q1).**\n  - Domain terms, dependencies, and unresolved decisions: \"Stale,\" \"warning,\"\n    \"data age,\" \"mandatory,\" \"report\" — all unresolved. See Q1–Q5.\n\n- **Verification contract**\n  - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus: **Open: cannot specify setup\n    without the threshold (Q1) and the reference event (Q5).**\n  - Observable evidence or oracle: The presence or absence of a staleness\n    warning on the report surface.\n  - Expected result: Warning is displayed when data age exceeds the threshold.\n    **Open: pass/fail boundary undefined.**\n  - Pass/fail criteria, including scope, thresholds, units, and timing:\n    **Open: threshold undefined (Q1).**\n  - Boundary, negative, and failure cases: Case where age equals threshold\n    exactly (boundary); case where age is below threshold (warning absent);\n    case where age data is unavailable. All unresolvable without Q1 and Q5.\n  - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence: A\n    verifiable timestamp or elapsed-time value observable at the report\n    boundary.\n  - Observable at the named boundary alone: yes — the warning is a visible\n    property of the report surface, provided the age value is also observable\n    there.\n  - If no, internal evidence needed and rationale: N/A (boundary-observable,\n    subject to the age value being surfaced).\n\n---\n\n## Suggested Supporting Requirements\n\n**SR-A — Boundary companion** (relates to Candidate 1)\n*Missing behavior:* What the report shall do when the data age cannot be\ndetermined (e.g., no timestamp is available). Without this, two implementers\nwould make different choices: one suppresses the warning, one shows it\nunconditionally.\n*Suggestion:* If the report cannot determine whether its data is current, then\nthe report shall display a staleness warning.\n*Reason:* Absence of an age value is arguably the most conservative case for\nstaleness and should be explicitly addressed before implementation.\n\n**SR-B — Required companion** (relates to Candidate 1, conditional on Q2)\n*Missing behavior:* If the warning is determined to be dismissible (Q2 =\noptional), a requirement is needed to define how and for how long a user may\nsuppress the warning, and whether the warning reappears on the next session or\nthe next threshold crossing.\n*Suggestion:* Add a companion requirement governing dismissal scope, persistence,\nand re-display conditions once the mandatory/optional decision is made.\n*Reason:* Without this companion, the dismissal behavior is undefined and\ntwo implementers will produce different results.\n\n**SR-C — Operational companion** (relates to Candidate 1)\n*Missing behavior:* The report data-age value must be observable at the report\nboundary for the staleness condition to be verifiable. If the age is not\ncurrently surfaced, a requirement to expose it may be needed.\n*Suggestion:* Consider whether a separate requirement is needed for the report\nto expose the data-refresh timestamp (or computed age) so that the staleness\ncondition can be independently verified.\n*Reason:* Without an observable age value, the staleness warning cannot be\nverified by an evaluator examining only the report boundary.\n\n---\n\n## Consistency Findings\n\n**Finding 1 — Gap: threshold is undefined**\nCandidate 1 cannot be reconciled with any other system behavior because the\nstaleness threshold is not defined. If a threshold is later introduced in a\ndifferent requirement (e.g., a data-refresh SLA), it should be confirmed\nwhether the staleness definition here must align with that value.\n\n**Finding 2 — Precedence question: mandatory vs. optional**\nIf the warning is optional (Q2), an explicit precedence is needed between the\n\"show warning\" obligation and any user preference or role-based permission to\nsuppress it. Without this, two valid interpretations conflict: one always shows\nthe warning to all users, one respects user-level suppression settings.\n\nNo conflicts or duplicates exist in the current candidate set because only one\ncandidate has been drafted.\n\n---\n\n## Assumptions\n\n**A1 (provisional):** \"The report\" refers to a single, identifiable system\ncomponent or UI surface. If multiple report types exist, this assumption must\nbe revisited.\n\n**A2 (provisional):** \"Age\" is a duration measured from a single observable\nreference event (e.g., last data refresh). If age is derived from multiple\nevents, the calculation rule must be defined.\n\n**A3 (provisional):** The staleness condition is evaluated at report-display\ntime, not at a scheduled interval. This assumption affects whether the\nrequirement is event-driven (triggered by display) or state-driven (maintained\ncontinuously). It must be confirmed by the product owner.\n\n---\n\n## Rationale and Context\n\nThe product owner's intent is to protect users from acting on outdated report\ndata. The warning is the proposed mechanism. The product owner has explicitly\ndeferred two decisions: the staleness threshold and whether the warning is\nmandatory. These are not implementation details; they are normative policy\nchoices that determine the EARS pattern, the normative sentence, and the\nverification criteria. They must be resolved before a normative requirement\ncan be finalized.\n\nThe source statement \"the report probably should show a warning\" uses modal\nlanguage (\"probably,\" \"should\") that signals deliberation, not an obligation.\nThis has been treated as a goal in need of clarification, not a normative\n`shall` obligation.\n\n---\n\n## Review Status\n\n| Item | Status | Blocking reason |\n|---|---|---|\n| Candidate 1 | needs clarification | Q1 (threshold), Q2 (mandatory/optional), Q3 (content), Q5 (reference event) all open; both contracts incomplete |\n| SR-A | suggestion | Pending acceptance and Q1/Q5 resolution |\n| SR-B | suggestion | Pending Q2 decision |\n| SR-C | suggestion | Pending Q4/interface definition |\n\n**No candidate is ready for review.** All candidates and supporting\nrequirements remain blocked until the product owner answers at minimum Q1\n(staleness threshold) and Q2 (mandatory vs. optional). Answering Q3\n(warning content) and Q5 (reference event) is also required to pass the\nimplementability and verification contracts.\n"},"output":"Created file successfully: artifacts/result.md","title":"write","metadata":{"metadata":{"truncated":false},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Created file successfully: artifacts/result.md"}],"providerCall":{"executed":false},"providerResult":{"executed":false},"rawInput":"{\"path\": \"/private/var/folders/qm/d729jn6n47z5nxpkpf361l9w0000gn/T/agent-eval/v2-regression/cases/case-014-uncertainty/artifacts/result.md\", \"content\": \"# Requirements Elicitation Package\\n\\n## Understanding\\n\\n**Requested outcome:** The report should display a warning to users when its\\ncontent may be out of date (stale). If age is not currently surfaced, a requirement to expose it may be needed.\n*Suggestion:* Consider whether a separate requirement is needed for the report to expose the data-refresh timestamp (or computed age) so that the staleness condition can be independently verified.\n*Reason:* Without an observable age value, an evaluator examining only the report boundary cannot verify the warning logic.\n\n---\n\n## Consistency Findings\n\n**Finding 1 — Gap: threshold is undefined**\nCandidate 1 cannot be reconciled with any other system behavior because the staleness threshold is not defined. Without this, two valid interpretations conflict: one always shows the warning to all users; one respects user-level suppression settings.\n\nNo conflicts or duplicates exist in the current candidate set because only one candidate has been drafted.\n\n---\n\n## Assumptions\n\n**A1 (provisional):** \"The report\" refers to a single, identifiable system component or UI surface. If age is derived from multiple events, the calculation rule must be defined.\n\n**A3 (provisional):** The staleness condition is evaluated at report-display time, not at a scheduled interval. This assumption affects whether the requirement is event-driven (triggered by display) or state-driven (maintained continuously). It must be confirmed by the product owner.\n\n---\n\n## Rationale and Context\n\nThe product owner's intent is to protect users from acting on outdated report data. # Requirements Elicitation Package

## Understanding

**Requested outcome:** A search system that returns matching records quickly,
presenting the newest matching records to the user after a search is submitted.

**Proposed system boundary:** The search system — the component that accepts a
user search submission and returns an ordered list of matching records.

**Design ideas embedded in the source (separated from obligations):**
The source proposes two specific implementation mechanisms:
- A Redis cache with a five-minute TTL
- GraphQL as the query interface

These are design choices, not externally observable behaviors. A verifier
cannot observe "Redis" or "GraphQL" at the user-facing boundary; they can
observe response latency, result ordering, and result freshness. These
implementation details are kept out of the normative sentences below.

**Behavioral obligations extracted from the source:**
1. When a user submits a search, the search system shall return matching
   records.
2. The results shall be ordered so that the newest matching records appear
   first.
3. Results shall return quickly (unquantified — flagged as needing
   clarification).

---

## Clarifying Questions

**Q1 (Candidate 1 — response time).** The source says results should return
"quickly." What is the maximum acceptable elapsed time, measured from when the
user submits a search to when the first results are visible? What threshold
distinguishes pass from fail, and does it differ for cached versus uncached
responses?

**Q2 (Candidate 2 — sort order definition).** "Newest" matching records: which
timestamp defines recency — record creation time, last-modification time, or
another field? If two records share the same timestamp, what is the tie-break
rule?

**Q3 (Candidate 2 — result set scope).** Should all matching records be
returned and sorted, or should the system return only a subset (for example, a
first page)? If a subset, what determines which records are included before
sorting?

**Q4 (Candidate 1 — what constitutes a "matching" record).** What makes a
record match a search? Is matching defined by full-text, field-level
comparison, prefix, relevance score, or another rule? The answer determines
whether the response is verifiable.

**Q5 (Candidate 1 — empty results).** When a submitted search matches no
records, what shall the system return? An empty result set, an informational
message, or some other response?

**Q6 (general — stale results acceptability).** The source implies results may
be served from a cache. Is it acceptable to return results that do not reflect
records created or modified after the cache was populated? If so, what is the
maximum acceptable staleness window?

---

## Candidate Requirements

### Candidate 1

- **Status:** needs clarification
- **Template:** Event-driven
- **Requirement:** When a user submits a search, the search system shall return
  all records that match the submitted search criteria within [unresolved:
  maximum response time].
- **Source intent and rationale:** The source requests that search results
  "return quickly." The user-visible obligation is that the system responds to
  a submitted search with matching records. The mechanism proposed in the source
  (Redis cache, GraphQL) is a design idea, not an observable behavior; it is
  kept out of the normative sentence. "Quickly" is unquantified and blocks the
  verification contract.
- **Implementability contract**
  - System boundary: The search system, at the interface visible to the
    submitting user.
  - Responsible system: Search system.
  - Actor: User (submitting a search).
  - Affected interfaces: The user-facing search interface (submission and
    response).
  - Inputs and data definitions: A submitted search — the specific form
    (keyword string, structured query, filters) is unresolved (see Q4). The
    record set to search is assumed to be the system's persistent record store;
    scope is unresolved.
  - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger: Trigger is user
    submission of a search. No precondition other than the system being
    operational is stated; authentication or authorization requirements are
    unresolved.
  - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response: Normal — a set of
    matching records is returned. Alternate — no matching records exist (see
    Q5, unresolved). Failure — system or dependency error response behavior is
    unresolved.
  - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances: Maximum
    acceptable elapsed time from submission to first results visible is
    unresolved (Q1). Whether the response is a complete set or a page is
    unresolved (Q3).
  - Domain terms, dependencies, and unresolved decisions: "Matching" is
    undefined (Q4). "Quickly" is unquantified (Q1). Acceptable result staleness
    is unresolved (Q6).
- **Verification contract**
  - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus: A populated record store; a user
    submits a search query.
  - Observable evidence or oracle: A response containing a set of records is
    returned at the user-facing boundary; elapsed time is measurable from
    submission to response receipt.
  - Expected result: The returned records all satisfy the match criterion;
    elapsed time is within the threshold.
  - Pass/fail criteria, including scope, thresholds, units, and timing:
    Unresolved — the response-time threshold (Q1) and the definition of
    "match" (Q4) must be established before pass/fail can be determined.
  - Boundary, negative, and failure cases: Zero-result searches (Q5),
    maximum record-set size, and dependency-failure behavior are unresolved.
  - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence: A timer
    measuring elapsed time from submission event to response receipt at the
    user boundary; a defined match oracle.
  - Observable at the named boundary alone: yes
  - If no, internal evidence needed and rationale: N/A

---

### Candidate 2

- **Status:** needs clarification
- **Template:** Event-driven
- **Requirement:** When a user submits a search, the search system shall
  present the matching records ordered by [unresolved: creation time |
  last-modification time | other timestamp] from newest to oldest.
- **Source intent and rationale:** The source states results should show "the
  newest matching records." This is a sort-order obligation on the result
  presentation. "Newest" is ambiguous — the timestamp field and tie-break rule
  are unresolved (Q2). "Show the newest" could also mean return only the top-N
  newest rather than all matches sorted; that scope question is unresolved (Q3).
- **Implementability contract**
  - System boundary: The search system, at the user-facing response boundary.
  - Responsible system: Search system.
  - Actor: User (receiving search results).
  - Affected interfaces: The user-facing result presentation interface.
  - Inputs and data definitions: The set of records matching the submitted
    search (as defined by Candidate 1). Each record must expose a timestamp
    field whose definition is unresolved (Q2).
  - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger: Trigger is the same
    user search submission as Candidate 1. The sort obligation applies to the
    result set produced in response to that submission.
  - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response: Normal — records are
    presented with the newest first. Alternate — a single matching record
    requires no ordering; an empty result set requires no ordering. Tie-break
    behavior for equal timestamps is unresolved (Q2).
  - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances: The timestamp
    field and its unit (epoch ms, ISO 8601, etc.) are unresolved. Whether all
    matches or only top-N are presented is unresolved (Q3).
  - Domain terms, dependencies, and unresolved decisions: "Newest" (Q2), scope
    of returned results (Q3), tie-break rule (Q2).
- **Verification contract**
  - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus: A record store containing multiple
    matching records with distinct and equal timestamps; a user submits a search
    that matches those records.
  - Observable evidence or oracle: The ordered sequence of records in the
    response, inspectable at the user-facing boundary.
  - Expected result: Records appear in descending timestamp order (newest
    first); tie-break ordering is consistent with the agreed rule.
  - Pass/fail criteria, including scope, thresholds, units, and timing:
    Unresolved — the timestamp field definition (Q2) and tie-break rule must be
    established. Pass requires that the first record in the response has a
    timestamp ≥ all others in the same response.
  - Boundary, negative, and failure cases: Single matching record; all records
    sharing the same timestamp; empty result set.
  - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence: Access to
    the timestamp field value of each returned record at the response boundary,
    or an agreed oracle that can evaluate ordering correctness.
  - Observable at the named boundary alone: yes, provided the timestamp field
    is included in the response.
  - If no, internal evidence needed and rationale: N/A

---

**S1 — Failure-path companion (Candidate 1).**
*Missing behavior:* What the search system shall do when a dependency required

unilaterally whether to reject, interpret, or pass through these inputs.

Unresolved — the timestamp field definition (Q2) and tie-break rule must be established. Pass requires that the first record in the response has a timestamp ≥ all others in the same response.

  • Boundary, negative, and failure cases: Single matching record; all records

sharing the same timestamp; empty result set.

  • Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence: Access to

the timestamp field value of each returned record at the response boundary, or an agreed oracle that can evaluate ordering correctness.

  • Observable at the named boundary alone: yes, provided the timestamp field

is included in the response.

  • If no, internal evidence needed and rationale: N/A

Suggested Supporting Requirements

S1 — Failure-path companion (Candidate 1). Missing behavior: What the search system shall do when a dependency required to produce results is unavailable (e.g., the record store is unreachable). Reason: Without a defined failure response, two implementers will choose different visible behaviors (error message, partial results, silent empty set), making the system unverifiable at the boundary. Suggested form (provisional): If the search system cannot retrieve records within [unresolved: timeout], then the search system shall return an error response that does not present partial results as complete.

S2 — Boundary companion (Candidate 1). Missing behavior: Behavior when the submitted search is empty, malformed, or exceeds a defined length limit. Reason: The source does not constrain the input. An implementer must decide unilaterally whether to reject, interpret, or pass through these inputs. Suggested form (provisional): If the submitted search criteria are empty or malformed, then the search system shall return an informative response that
